summary: Client SDK connection throttling causes head-of-line blocking and token-stream stalls
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports intermittent but sustained token streaming slowdowns and timeouts for streaming completions beginning 2026-03-09 18:00 UTC. Affected endpoints exhibit high tail latency and frequent stream reconnects. Impact: customer-facing product metrics show 18% drop in perceived responsiveness and several errors surfaced in client logs (stream closed by server / request timed out).

Impact:
- QueryFlow's chat product shows 15-25% of streaming requests with >2s token latency (p99 ~1.8s).
- Several sessions observed multiple partial responses and reconnects, degrading UX.
- Customer on Dedicated pool; requests routed to us-east serving fleet.

Environment:
- Customer tier: dedicated
- Region: us-east-1
- SDK: redwood-js v2.2.0 (self-managed configuration in product), Node 18 runtime
- Backend: Redwood hosted dedicated GPUs (serving-runtime rev 2026-02-28), API gateway cluster ag-14

Steps to reproduce:
1) Configure the SDK with default connection pool settings (maxConnectionsPerHost: 6, maxIdle: 2) and maxRetries: 4.
2) Start 200 concurrent streaming chat sessions from the customer service (each session issues ~3 parallel streaming requests over time).
3) Observe p50/p95/p99 token latencies reported by the SDK and compare to baseline.
4) Capture network traces and SDK connection pool metrics (connection_acquire_wait_ms, inflight_streams_per_conn).

Observed logs / traces:
- SDK stack traces show repeated HTTP acquire timeouts: "connection_acquire_timeout after 2000ms" followed by retry/backoff.
- API gateway shows short bursts of 429s and 503s while serving-runtime logs show no OOMs but elevated connection close counts.
- NGINX-proxy metrics show many keepalive connections being frequently closed with TIME_WAIT.
- Traces reveal long head-of-line wait times in SDK: requests queued waiting for an available socket; once a connection freed, multiple queued requests race and trigger serialized backoffs.

Initial hypothesis:
- SDK connection pool sized too conservatively for customer's concurrency pattern combined with aggressive retry/backoff configuration leads to request queueing in SDK.
- HTTP/2 multiplexing not used effectively because SDK falls back to HTTP/1.1 per-request semantics (customer's load balancer TLS session reuse disabled).
- Combined effect: head-of-line blocking at client layer appears as token-level streaming slowness even though serving runtime responds promptly when requests hit it.

Temporary workarounds (recommended to customer on 2026-03-10):
- Increase SDK maxConnectionsPerHost to 40 and maxIdle to 10 for service processes handling chat streaming.
- Reduce maxRetries to 2 and add larger jitter to backoff to avoid synchronized retry storms.
- Enable HTTP/2 in the load balancer and ensure TLS session reuse so SDK can open fewer long-lived multiplexed connections.

Note: Customer applied increased pool settings and saw immediate reduction in queueing; p99 token latency dropped from ~1.8s to ~220ms in a controlled test.

investigation_notes: Metric correlation: SDK connection_acquire_wait_ms spikes align with customer-reported p99 token latency windows; serving-runtime request_latency remained steady except for small queuing jitter when requests actually arrived.
Reproduced locally with synthetic load: with default pool settings p99 token latency 1.6s; with increased pool and HTTP/2 multiplexing enabled p99 token latency 200ms.
Heap and GC traces from Node processes show no leaks. Problem is I/O contention at client-side socket pool and retry amplification.
Observed repeated retry storms: multiple requests hit acquire timeout roughly simultaneously, then backoff schedule clusters causing periodic retry surges that temporarily saturate available sockets.

SRE note: NGINX keepalive timeout on LB was 30s; combined with session reuse disabled this produced high socket churn. Recommend increasing keepalive and enabling TLS session reuse for long-lived streaming clients.

Related support ticket SUP-32011 documents a previous case of client-side pool saturation but differences: that ticket was HTTP/2 stream-exhaustion; here the chain is acquire-timeouts + retry synchronization on HTTP/1.1 fallback.
Linked github: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/502 contains proposed SDK defaults and backoff change.
resolution:
Workaround and short-term fix applied: customer increased SDK pool limits and reduced retries; internal LB change enabled HTTP/2 passthrough for streaming paths. SDK v2.3.1 released with safer defaults: maxConnectionsPerHost=32, maxIdle=8, default maxRetries=2, randomized exponential jitter. Runtime team applied LB TLS settings change in us-east cluster.

Follow-ups and actions:
- SDK team to publish guidance and upgrade notice in README and changelog (assigned to SDK PM, due 2026-03-18).
- Add automated alert for connection_acquire_wait_ms > 500ms tied to customer onboarding checks (SRE action item INT-4067).
- Postmortem scheduled: 2026-03-15; include documentation updates and a short customer-facing bulletin summarizing root cause and recommendations.

Status: Mitigations applied and customer confirmed improved UX. Ticket remains In Progress until postmortem and SDK docs update are complete.
